title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
prompt:
Given points on a plane, connect them all with minimum total cost, where the cost between two points is their Manhattan distance `|x1-x2| + |y1-y2|`. Return the minimum total.

**Example**: `[[0,0],[2,2],[3,10],[5,2],[7,0]]` → `20`.

This is a Minimum Spanning Tree. Prim's algorithm with a min-heap grows the tree one cheapest edge at a time.
hints: Prim's MST: a min-heap of `{cost, node}`, plus a visited array.
Start from node 0 at cost 0. Pop the cheapest unvisited node, add its cost, then push edges to all still-unvisited nodes.
Stop once all n nodes are in the tree.

solution.explanation: The graph is complete (any two points connectable), so Prim's is natural: repeatedly absorb the nearest point not yet in the tree. The heap always surfaces the cheapest frontier edge; skipping already-in-MST pops handles stale entries. O(n² log n).
